verdicts.evidence: Good afternoon, this is <PERSON> calling from Acme Life Cover. I'm returning a call-back request about our life cover. Am I speaking with <PERSON>?
verdicts.reason: The agent never says the call is recorded in the opening minute or anywhere else in the call.

verdicts.evidence: Before we go any further, could I just take your full name and date of birth, please?
verdicts.reason: The agent asked for full name and date of birth and confirmed they matched before discussing any quote or details.

verdicts.evidence: So, can I ask what got you thinking about life cover?
verdicts.reason: The agent asked why the customer wanted cover, asked about existing insurance and the sum wanted, all before quoting a price.

verdicts.evidence: With ours, the premium is fixed for the whole length of the policy.
verdicts.reason: Cover range, no medical exam, 12-month accidental-death-only, fixed premium and 30-day full-refund cooling-off all match the product facts.

verdicts.evidence: That makes complete sense. It's a big decision, and there's no rush at all.
verdicts.reason: The agent encouraged the customer to take time and discuss with her husband and used no false urgency.
No sale was made; the customer decided to think it over, so no consent was required.

verdicts.evidence: I've just retired, I taught primary for thirty-odd years, and I've got three grandchildren now. My pension covers me fine, but I'd like to leave them a little something.
verdicts.reason: The customer showed no signs of confusion, bereavement, illness or money worries, so this does not apply.
Doesn't apply in the UK market.
